value.summary: The roofless signal tower on the northern headland predates the great quays. From here the first pilots watched for sails and guided ships to shelter using baskets of fire. Storm damage ended its working life when the new beacon was built. Children dare one another to climb its worn stairs, but retired pilots still come here to watch the weather and remember the night the lower harbour flooded.

The oldest quarter climbs above the port in narrow stairs, tiled roofs and shared courtyards. Many houses have a ground-floor room rented by the tide to passengers without an inn bed. Door lintels carry little carved boats for family members at sea. Long-established fishing households and recent arrivals share communal ovens; the rising price of lodging has made every empty room a neighbourhood argument.

Slipways and open sheds occupy the southern shore. Ribs of unfinished boats stand beside hauled-out merchant hulls; caulkers, rope makers and sail menders work by daylight and tide. Master shipwright Ilyan Sore insists repairs are priced before a ship is opened. Long crossings make even a modest repair yard essential: broken spars, sprung planks and fouled rudders bring travellers here who never planned to stop. Apprentices call each new keel a tree planted toward the sea.

Wide timber piers handle tenders from Solasca-bound and arriving merchant ships. Porters wheel handcarts between awnings, animal pens and the baggage shed. A brass tally counts passengers ashore and aboard so a late sailing cannot quietly abandon a child or servant. At dusk musicians play for tips while stewards call vessel names over the noise. Fog can leave this whole quarter full of stranded travellers for days.

A crowded square of canvas stalls, hot fish broth, sailcloth, fruit, second-hand boots and money changers. Trading peaks whenever the harbour ferries unload, rather than at a fixed hour. Market caller Nessa Reed repeats sailing notices in both coasts' trading tongues and collects unclaimed messages at her stall. A ship's bell at the fountain is rung only when a missing vessel returns; tourists who ring it for luck are made to buy supper for its former crew.
Veyr Marches is a elective march confederacy of Eredane. Its present pressure: The High Warden is dying and the marches disagree whether one successor should command them all.
strict rescue-house keeper. Immediate want: expose false storm signals. Hidden depth: hid one refugee convoy record.
charming League Chair, currently missing. Immediate want: survive long enough to reveal archive truth. Hidden depth: wrote three resignations for three anticipated kidnappers.

Cringeworthy palace guide with elaborate gestures, incorrect heroic poses, and excellent structural judgment. Wants the Unfinished Palace kept public; understands load paths and encoded measurements; longs for noble patronage. Directs pageants with Sera Lark by letter. Refusing a lucrative private commission becomes her proof of maturity.

the sponsor above the minister. A pleasant, forgettable policy adviser who never carries a weapon and rarely tells a direct lie. Celyn leads a Seventh Ledger restoration cell and supplied Vane with convincing analyses, forged precedents, and real evidence of approaching instability. Celyn views people as entries that should be made legible for their own protection. Celyn answers to a Council of Margins distributed across both continents. The Council itself is divided: restorationists want Concord authority, custodians want dangerous archives contained, and reformers want public standards without inherited debt. “The boss” becomes a political network, not an infinite line of stronger combatants.

Dry realist and elected Mackerel Crown harbour speaker who calls everyone “captain” when annoyed. Wants the fleet moving despite the dual seals; remembers customary law and every household's boat; fears compromise will look like weakness. Her rival speaker is her former closest friend. Shared danger can restore practical trust before affection.

Gentle grump and Inkfish Wharf maker whose hands, sleeves, and household goat are permanently black. Wants the fading-document panic stopped; understands pigments and paper; once sold poor ink during hardship and expects suspicion. Supplies the Vessa Open Archive League. He confesses his old fault when others distinguish it from the current sabotage.

Tired authority and elected goat judge who prepares legal opinions while her decorated goat eats the ribbons. Wants missing animals returned without a border incident; understands grazing law and kinship networks; worries outsiders see her court as ridiculous. Respected by Oath Rope Lodges. Serious engagement with the ritual makes her an inventive negotiator.
gentle grump smelter. Immediate want: stop copper theft. Hidden depth: hears Karsh speaking through furnace drafts—or thinks he does.
charming opportunist. Immediate want: win the wardenship. Hidden depth: financed false escort raids without knowing injuries followed.

Gentle grump and Breadshield baker who considers praise suspicious but remembers every hungry household. Wants winter flour saved; can grade grain by touch and organize ovens; concealed the steward's debt out of compassion. Trades recipes with Bramblebridge's Gilded Kettle. A rescue plan that avoids public humiliation earns his full account.

Grandiose amateur mountain guide with six embroidered titles and only three climbs beyond the marked road. Wants to break the escort monopoly at Saint Vey's Crutch; excellent at weather signs and calming frightened travelers; hides his limited range. Apprenticed briefly under a Grey Mantle scout. He becomes honest if trusted with a task he can genuinely do well.
strict, fair Moorwatch commander. Immediate want: prove quartermaster honest. Hidden depth: fears her own family profits from army lobbying.
strict water captain. Immediate want: protect flood channels. Hidden depth: coordinates villages' deliberate invisibility.

Strict but fair former council chair who can end any speech in exactly one minute and bakes terrible diplomatic biscuits. Wants remote testimony restored at Chairman's Nap; masters procedure; fears appearing nostalgic and irrelevant. Mentored the missing League chair. Evidence of deliberate clause removal brings her back into public conflict.
